The commercial problem

Pretty aerials are not enough when size is the story.

Land and development campaigns repeatedly generate the same early questions: how large is the holding, where does the boundary run, what is the frontage and how does the site sit in its surrounding context? A marketing image that carries those answers can do more work than a generic drone photograph.

This is why Sixth Vision Commercial combines photography with measured site, boundary, frontage and amenity mapping where the campaign needs it.

What was delivered

Photography and information, designed as one asset.

01 · Aerial frame

The property is shown from above at dusk, preserving both site scale and visual campaign impact.

02 · Boundary run

The site perimeter is made legible directly on the image rather than forcing the viewer to cross-reference another document.

03 · Dimensions

Key boundary measurements are placed where they can be read immediately in the marketing frame.

Why this matters

The frame becomes part of the sales conversation.

For an agent, developer or owner, measured aerial media can make a site easier to explain on portals, in brochures, in an information memorandum and in direct enquiry follow-up. It does not replace survey or legal documentation; it makes the campaign more legible.
